markdown:
## The True Cost of Hiring

Many organizations understate what a hire costs, because they count only the invoices. When you include internal time and ramp-up, the true figure is usually higher than the visible one. We quote no industry average here, because we have not cited a source for one. Calculate your own.

### What Gets Missed

Most cost-per-hire calculations include:

- Job board postings
- Agency fees, if used
- Background checks

But they often miss:

- Recruiter salary, allocated per hire
- Hiring manager time
- Interview team time
- Offer and negotiation time
- Onboarding costs
- Productivity ramp-up

### The Complete Formula

True cost per hire = (external costs + internal costs) / total hires

External costs:

- Job boards and advertising
- Agency or vendor fees
- Background checks and assessments
- Recruitment marketing
- ATS and tool subscriptions

Internal costs:

- Recruiter salary and benefits (the share of time spent on hiring)
- Hiring manager time (hours multiplied by hourly cost)
- Interview panel time
- HR and onboarding staff time
- Training and ramp-up investment

### An Illustrative Example

*Illustrative example only. This is a hypothetical company hiring 50 people a year. Every figure is an assumption for demonstration, not a benchmark and not a result for any client. Replace each input with your own.*

| Cost category | Assumption | Annual total | Per hire |
|---|---|---|---|
| Job boards | Assumed annual spend | $50,000 | $1,000 |
| One recruiter | Assumed fully loaded cost | $80,000 | $1,600 |
| Manager time | 10 hours per hire at an assumed $75 per hour | $37,500 | $750 |
| Interview time | 5 hours x 4 people at an assumed $50 per hour | $50,000 | $1,000 |
| Onboarding | Assumed annual spend | $25,000 | $500 |
| **Total** | | **$242,500** | **$4,850** |

This leaves out agency fees. Add even occasional agency use and the total rises. Run the same arithmetic with your own numbers before comparing options. See [pricing](/pricing) for how TaaSFlow charges.

### Where a Subscription Model May Help

Some employers prefer a defined fee for a defined search to variable placement fees. TaaSFlow is a recruiting platform with managed execution. Agents source and score candidates, a recruiter reviews every shortlist before you see it, and you make every hiring decision. Whether it lowers your cost per hire depends on how many roles you fill and how you use it, so run the calculation above for both options. It is not the right fit for every search.

### Strategies for Reducing Cost-Per-Hire

- **Improve source quality:** stop spending on low-converting channels
- **Speed up the process:** time is a cost for everyone involved
- **Build referral programs:** often a low-cost source
- **Invest in employer brand:** can reduce the need for expensive sourcing
- **Compare fee models:** look at the whole cost, not only the invoice line

### Track and Optimize

Measure cost per hire regularly. Break it down by department, role type and source. Identify outliers and address root causes.

The goal is not just lower cost. It is a better return on your talent investment.
